transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because things at work have been getting… strange. Ever since I got that county safety award, some people there have been twisting my inspection reports, like making them look off, and then asking these pointed budget questions like they’re trying to make me look crooked.

My supervisor keeps saying it’s just normal review, but it doesn’t feel normal. I can tell there’s a coordinated effort to discredit me.
Can you tell me more about why you believe your coworkers are trying to discredit you? Have you noticed any specific actions or evidence that supports this belief?

Yeah. It started after I got that county safety award. Before that, my reports were just my reports, you know? But after that, certain people started going through them and making it seem like there were problems where there weren’t.

They’ll ask these pointed questions about budgets or why I wrote something a certain way, like they’re setting me up to look like I’m doing something crooked. My supervisor says it’s just normal review, but it doesn’t feel that way to me. It feels coordinated, like they’re trying to undermine me and make me look bad.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood, like feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, especially around the time this started happening at work?

I don’t know… I wouldn’t say I’ve been hopeless or anything like that. I mean, it’s been stressful, yeah, and I think about it a lot because it’s happening at work. But I haven’t really noticed being down or losing interest in things the way you’re asking.
Have you noticed times when you’ve felt unusually energetic, needed less sleep, or been more talkative than usual, like your thoughts are racing or you’re on a ‘high’?

No, I don’t think so. I haven’t had times where I’m on some kind of high or not needing sleep. I mean, I can get worked up thinking about what’s going on at work, but that’s not the same as feeling unusually energetic or racing like that.
